takeaways.label: Two engines, not one
takeaways.text: Corporate advisory and capital markets rebounded sharply from a near-dead April–May, while private markets disbursements doubled to ₹977 crores as equity choppiness pushed activity toward credit.

takeaways.label: The pipeline is the story: ₹130,000 crores
takeaways.text: of transactions already filed with the regulator for execution over the next 12 months, with more filings expected this quarter and next.

takeaways.label: Leverage has bottomed
takeaways.text: Management "confidently" called the bottom on private markets debt-equity at 0.8x and expects to start borrowing from next quarter itself.

takeaways.label: Wealth profitability slips a year
takeaways.text: Full-year break-even now expected in FY28, a delay of three to four quarters, because transactional income volatility slowed revenue growth.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the ₹130,000 crore pipeline converts at the promised pace, the first drawdown of the Pre-IPO Fund, and any buyback signal once the NSE lockup expires in March 2027.

points.label: Sharp revival from a dead start
points.text: April and May were "really horrible months" with literally no deals going through; activity started in June and July, August, September were very good.

points.label: Ranked #1 across IPOs and QIPs
points.text: Closed transactions of ₹83,000 crores in Q2, with a significant portion of deals trading up post-listing.

points.label: Revenue left on the table
points.text: Approximately ₹45–50 crores of revenue was lost because deal sizes were reduced in the difficult environment; ₹10,000 crores reduction in deal size last quarter versus what was filed with the regulator.

points.label: ROE is structurally extreme
points.text: The segment operates "almost an infinite ROE" because capital is just profit ploughed back and kept as cash; it needs no incremental capital to grow.

points.label: Growth is compounding, not linear
points.text: Profitability is expected to grow at 15%–20% from a peak-to-peak perspective, with a new peak every four to five years.

quotes.text: Kampani: "April, May were really horrible months because we literally had no deals going through. The activity really started in June. I would think 15% is a very reasonable number to assume for the rest of the year, especially after the kind of the market lift that we have seen today and the results of the U.S. election."

points.label: Disbursements doubled to ₹977 crores
points.text: in Q2, primarily in the bespoke category, because equity market choppiness drove more action on the credit side.

points.label: Bespoke book grew ₹800 crores to ₹3,800 crores
points.text: , with a significant portion in the two-to-three-year maturity bucket, not short-term.

points.label: Cash fell from ₹3,077 crores to ₹1,691 crores
points.text: , largely because of disbursements and repayment of some borrowings without needing to borrow significantly.

points.label: Debt-equity has bottomed at 0.8x
points.text: Management will need to start borrowing from next quarter itself due to planned disbursements and potential prepayments on the wholesale side.

points.label: Cash floor is explicit
points.text: Management will always maintain at least ₹1,000 crores of pure cash for ALM structure and opportunities.

points.label: Real estate book is stable, not growing
points.text: , because pricing is a challenge; management requires at least 200–300 bps pricing above corporate, which the market resists.

points.label: Yield drop explained
points.text: The drop in yield is absolutely because the LAS book went up, real estate stayed stable, and the overall book fell.

points.label: Discipline over volume
points.text: Management will not do deals where risk-adjusted returns are not liked; lumpy quarters are acceptable.

quotes.text: Kampani: "If we feel we cannot syndicate, then we will not do it here."

points.label: One very large account resolved
points.text: Final NCLT approval came through in October, giving over almost ₹330–340 crores of liquidity before close of this quarter.

points.label: SR investments came down to almost ₹2,825 crores
points.text: , with ₹350 crores of cash resolution to JM, totaling almost ₹ 800 crores of resolution this quarter.

points.label: Gain timing is split
points.text: Some of the gain from the October resolution is already factored into fair value changes reported quarter-on-quarter, but some will come this quarter.

points.label: More SR deployment ahead
points.text: Management sees a lot of interesting retail portfolios from a number of NBFCs and will look to invest more on the SR side.

points.label: Resolution pipeline is quantified
points.text: ARC will look to resolve over ₹2,000 crores in SR investments and get cash back over the next 18 months to two years, with returns modeled at around 16%–18%.

points.label: Volatility will reduce structurally
points.text: As ARC adds more retail granular assets, earnings volatility will reduce considerably over the next few years.

points.label: Gokaldas Exports is a deliberate hold
points.text: The merged ARC asset suffered due to U.S. tariffs, but management wants to stay invested long-term despite quarterly mark-to-market volatility.

points.label: Recurring AUM and loans grew ~17% to almost ₹40,000 crores
points.text: , with focus on improving productivity.

points.label: Wealth business broke even in September
points.text: , driven by both recurring revenues and some transaction revenues.

points.label: Headcount rationalization was internal
points.text: Loss in RMs is purely on productivity basis, planned to create a sharper sales franchise; "not stuff that we have lost to the market or competition."

points.label: Recruitment cycle is deliberate
points.text: Over the last 36 months there was a lot of recruitment; the last six months focused on productivity. The cycle is 18 months to two years of strong recruitment, then one to one-and-a-half years of making it productive.

points.label: Full-year profitability delayed to FY28
points.text: , roughly three to four quarters from original plan, because transactional income volatility in the last six to nine months reduced revenue growth.

points.label: Pre-IPO Fund first close at ₹700+ crores
points.text: , with first investment expected to be announced very shortly.

points.label: Singapore VCC scaled from zero to over \$225 million
points.text: in 18 months, primarily driven by internal distribution.

points.label: AMC AUM largely flat sequentially
points.text: SIP book came down from ₹90 crores to ₹87 crores because small-cap, mid-cap, and flexi-cap schemes saw volatility from macro and concentrated calls.

points.label: Performing credit fund fully drawn down
points.text: , with roadshows on for the second performing credit fund; first close expected this quarter.

quotes.text: Kampani: "The magic of a strong distribution and the flywheel pushing hard into the manufactured products is working pretty well."

points.label: H1 private markets revenue up 63% YoY
points.text: to ₹582 crores, driven by strong underlying growth excluding write-backs.

points.label: Operating PBT roughly flat H1 vs H1
points.text: , because last year had ₹231 crores write-back versus only ₹15 crores this year so far; excluding write-backs, operating PBT grew ~60%.

points.label: Write-backs are targeted at ₹250 crores this year
points.text: , on track to close by March 31, with more expected in the next six to nine months.

points.label: Interim dividend increased 10%
points.text: from ₹1.5 to ₹1.65 per share; total payout ₹7.6 per share over last six quarters, representing ₹727 crores.

points.label: Buyback is constrained, not ruled out
points.text: A significant portion of liquidity is in NBFCs, and taking it out would incur a tax hit at the holding company level before a buyback. NSE stock is subject to a six-month lockup expiring March 2027. Management will take the call in April/May next year.

points.label: ROE target is mid-teens
points.text: toward the end of the investment cycle of many businesses.

points.label: Profit growth should outpace revenue
points.text: If revenue growth is 15–20%, profit growth should be 20–25% as more operating scale is achieved.

quotes.text: Kampani: "Fundamentally, one issue we have is that a significant portion of the liquidity that we have is in the NBFCs, and we've chosen to deploy that into business over the last one year because there is no method of taking out this liquidity from the NBFCs without having a tax hit first at a holding company level before we implement a buyback."

points.label: Demerger is on the table, not on the clock
points.text: Management has thought about spinning off wealth management, asset management, or wealth management and corporate advisory together "many times" but wants to focus on execution and scale before any restructuring.

points.label: The trigger is size
points.text: Wealth management and asset management need to become larger before a demerger makes sense; decision deferred to "the right time" without a timeline.

points.label: Capital markets ROE argues for separation
points.text: , but management is not moving yet.

quotes.text: Kampani: "We have thought about this many times in the last few years. We just want to focus on execution and scale these businesses before going into any restructuring, which could be something earlier than we need to do it."

items.title: IPO/ECM pipeline monetisation
items.text: JM ranked #1 in IPOs and QIPs in Q2 FY27, closing 26 transactions worth over ₹83,000 crore, with ₹1,30,000 crore of deals already filed with SEBI for execution over the next 12 months and more being filed. Advisory revenue jumped 2.5x QoQ to ₹286 crore in Q2 with ~36% annualised ROE, and management expects a 12-18 month execution window with 15-20% profit growth over the next couple of years.

items.title: Private Markets re-leveraging
items.text: Standard loans grew 22% YoY to ₹4,748 crore with Q2 disbursements doubling YoY to ₹977 crore at ~13% yields, and management targets 15-20% annual book growth toward ₹7,000-8,000 crore in three years. Debt-equity bottomed at 0.8x and borrowing restarts from next quarter, climbing back to ~2x within three years to lift segment ROE from 10.7% toward the 12-13% target.

items.title: ARC resolution cash waterfall
items.text: Roughly ₹2,000 crore of security receipt investments remain to be resolved and converted to cash over the next 18 months to two years at 16-18% returns, after gross resolutions crossed ₹2,000 crore in Q1 FY27 and ~₹800 crore in Q2. The ARC expects to be debt-free within six months, after which its cash safely compounds at 16-18% IRR, and retail NPA portfolios from NBFCs offer granular new acquisition growth.

items.title: Wealth Management breakeven and productivity
items.text: The wealth business broke even in September FY27, with standalone full-year profitability targeted in FY28 and 20-25% business growth guided for FY27. Recurring AUM of ₹37,000 crore is up 16% YoY and recurring revenue up 20%, while the completed 100+ RM recruitment cycle shifts to productivity - new recurring assets yield over 60 bps versus the ~35 bps book average, driving operating leverage.

items.title: Affordable home loans scale-up
items.text: AUM grew 30% YoY to ₹4,000 crore with 48% disbursement growth in Q2 FY27 across 152 branches, spreads widened to 4.8% and GNPA fell to 1.1%, with 25-30% AUM growth guided for the next three years. A separate listing is targeted by 2028-29, and Bajaj Life Insurance's ₹65 crore stake purchase at ~₹3,100 crore valuation benchmarks the business ahead of that.

items.title: Alternatives fund raises
items.text: The maiden pre-IPO fund achieved a first close of over ₹700 crore toward a ₹1,000+ crore target, with a PE fund to launch immediately after at a similar size; the second performing credit fund's first close is expected within FY27. AIF AUM has already grown 3.2x YoY to ₹1,063 crore, and a ₹150 crore AMC investment over two years aims to take mutual fund AUM toward ₹25,000 crore from ~₹14,000 crore average.

items.title: Singapore VCC and Abu Dhabi entry
items.text: The Singapore variable capital company scaled from zero 18 months ago to over $225 million AUM, adding $30-40 million of net assets a quarter through internal distribution. JM Financial (Middle East) was incorporated in ADGM on 12 October 2026 to arrange deals, advise and manage assets, extending the offshore wealth platform to Gulf clients.
